title: Short exactness of the fixed right external Cech sequences
statement: For a field $k$, schemes $X,Y$ over $k$ with affine diagonal [lem-sc-picard-affine-diagonal-intersections], finite families of affine opens $U,V$, a quasi-coherent $F$ on $X$ and a short exact sequence $S$ of quasi-coherent modules on $Y$, the two functorially constructed sequences $S.map(A)$ and $S.map(B)$ of [def-sc-picard-external-right-cech-models] are short exact. No cover condition is required.

source.place: Tag 0BED, equation-kunneth-on-cech (33.29.1.1) and the following coefficient sequence diagram; official tag page read

proof.text: Finite tuple intersections are affine by the affine diagonal criterion. Quasi-coherent sections preserve a short exact sequence there: left exactness gives the kernel and affine vanishing gives surjectivity. Scalar restriction and finite products preserve this exactness.

For A, tensor each section sequence with a factor term over the field and take the finite sum in a total degree. For B, identify sections on each product intersection with the tensor of factor sections by the affine product, pullback and tensor formulas. Both complexes are degreewise short exact; extension by zero gives zero sequences in negative degrees. Apply degreewise short exactness of complexes. This includes empty index families.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BED, explicit fixed Cech models and the right-variable version of the coefficient diagram

lean.statement:
theorem picardExternal_right_cech_exact
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal g)]
    {ι κ : Type w} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (V : κ → Y.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hV : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (S : ShortComplex Y.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [S.X₁.IsQuasicoherent] [S.X₂.IsQuasicoherent] [S.X₃.IsQuasicoherent]
    : (S.map (picardRightTensorCechFunctor f g U V F)).ShortExact ∧
      (S.map (picardRightProductCechFunctor f g U V F)).ShortExact
